_README: Authored rulings for the New Year's Concert sidecar. AUTHORITY: applied LAST by
tools/prep_exhibit_concerts.py, never rewritten by it. COMMITTED, unlike the
Two uses: (1) rule on a programme-contradiction the tool reported (the two
archives disagree; see the report), (2) supply a concert the archives predate
(2024 onwards). Every entry needs `_disposition` ('editorial' — a ruling; or
'until-upstream-fixed' — an archive error), a `source` naming where the fact
was checked, and `"verified": true` once a person has checked it. UNVERIFIED
ENTRIES ARE NOT APPLIED: the tool names them on every run instead.
Fields patch the year's entry as generated: `conductor`, `date`, `title`,
`programme` (the whole list), `note`. A contradiction is ruled PER ITEM instead:
`items` maps the report's item number to a ruling — `take` names the archive the
arbiter agrees with ('philharmoniker' = the reading shown, 'musikverein' = the
`alt`), and `credit`, `title`, `opus` override field by field, derived exactly as
an archive's own entry would be. Keys starting with `_` are notes, never applied.

1946._what: item 7, Persischer Marsch, op. 289 — composer: orchestra 'Johann Strauß II.' vs Musikverein 'Josef Strauß'
1946._prior: From memory, UNVERIFIED — the book rules. Op. 289 is Johann Strauss II's Persischer Marsch (1864); Josef Strauss wrote no Persian march. Lean: orchestra (as shown). Confidence: high.
1946.source: Kurt Dieman-Dichtl, Wiens goldener Klang, p. ? (page to fill)

1949._what: item 9 — orchestra 'Neue Pizzicato-Polka. op. 449' (Johann Strauß II.) vs Musikverein 'Pizzicato-Polka' (Johann Strauß Sohn / Josef Strauß)
1949._prior: No prior. Two DIFFERENT works: the Neue Pizzicato-Polka op. 449 (Johann II alone, from Fürstin Ninetta, 1893) and the joint Pizzicato-Polka of 1869 (Johann II and Josef, no opus). Only the book, or the 1949 programme leaflet, can say which was played. Set take to philharmoniker if the book agrees with the orchestra, musikverein if it names the joint polka.
1949.source: Kurt Dieman-Dichtl, Wiens goldener Klang, p. ? (page to fill)

1950._what: item 6 — orchestra 'Aurora-Polka, op. 165' vs Musikverein 'Auroraball. Polka française, op. 219' (both Johann Strauß II.)
1950._prior: From memory, UNVERIFIED — the book rules. Op. 165 is the Aurora-Polka (1855); op. 219 is the Auroraball-Tänze, a WALTZ (1859) — the Musikverein's 'Polka française, op. 219' pairs one work's genre with the other's opus, which reads as a conflation. Lean: orchestra (as shown). Confidence: low.
1950.source: Kurt Dieman-Dichtl, Wiens goldener Klang, p. ? (page to fill)

2004._prior: From memory, UNVERIFIED — the book rules. Eislauf, Polka schnell op. 261 is Josef Strauss's (1869); Johann Strauss I's numbered works end at op. 251, so an op. 261 of his cannot exist. Lean: Musikverein. Confidence: high.
